title: Five-Minute Quickstart
content:
1. docker compose up -d
2. curl http://localhost:14800/readyz
3. curl http://localhost:14800/v1/version to inspect feature flags
4. PUT /v1/facts to store a fact
5. POST http://localhost:14801/mcp with tools/list to verify MCP
6. corecruxctl verify-store --data-dir ./data

title: Local-Only Mode
content: If sync_status reports mode=local_only or mode=degraded, do not block the user. CoreCrux Community Edition still provides a local fact store, local session store, HTTP API, and MCP tools on this node. Continue storing facts and sessions locally, tell the user remote sync is not available yet, and only treat sync as optional follow-up work.

title: Choosing HTTP vs MCP
content: Use HTTP when the host system needs shared app state or service-to-service calls: /v1/facts, /v1/sessions, /v1/version. Use MCP when the agent needs private facts, agent-scoped sessions, handoff, or tool discovery. Many systems use both: HTTP for shared product data and MCP for per-agent memory.

title: Human-Assisted Integration
content: Use this when the agent cannot edit the host system directly. 1. Ask the operator which surface they need: HTTP, MCP, or both. 2. Give them the exact endpoint, auth token/header, and env vars to set. 3. Tell them to verify with /v1/version for HTTP and tools/list or get_agent_identity for MCP. 4. Finish by storing and retrieving one fact as an end-to-end check.

title: Automatic Integration
content: Use this when the agent can edit the host application or runtime config. 1. Detect whether the target integration needs shared HTTP state, MCP agent memory, or both. 2. Write the base URL, auth config, and MCP bearer token into the target system. 3. Reload or restart the host application. 4. Verify with /v1/version, tools/list, store_fact, and query_facts. 5. If remote sync is desired later, add CORECRUXD_SYNC_REMOTE_URL and CORECRUXD_SYNC_API_KEY, then re-check sync_status.

title: Appending Events
content: POST /v1/admin/append (or compatibility alias /v1/append) with tenant_id, stream_type, stream_id, and events array. Each event needs event_id, occurred_at (RFC3339), event_type, and payload (JSON string). Default Community Edition runtime leaves the dataplane disabled, so append requires a dataplane-enabled deployment.

title: Text Search
content: POST /v1/query/text-search with tenant_id and query. Optional: token_budget (fill until budget), min_score (relevance floor), mode=scan (metadata only).

title: Fact Store
content: PUT /v1/facts to store. GET /v1/facts?query=... to search. GET /v1/facts/entity/{name} by entity. DELETE /v1/facts/{id} to soft-delete.

title: Session Store
content: PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/state with JSON body. GET /v1/sessions/{id}/state to retrieve. State persists across requests within the session.

title: Architecture
content: 14 Rust crates. corecruxd serves HTTP on 14800, gRPC on 4007, and built-in MCP on 14801 by default. Append-only event store with sealed segments. .ccxi companion indexes for BM25. CROWN receipts on every operation.

title: Configuration
content: All config via environment variables. CORECRUXD_DATA_DIR (data), CORECRUXD_HTTP_PORT (default 14800), CORECRUXD_BUILD_CCXI (index building), CORECRUXD_QUERY_TEXT_SEARCH (enable search). Optional upstream sync uses CORECRUXD_SYNC_ENABLED, CORECRUXD_SYNC_REMOTE_URL, CORECRUXD_SYNC_API_KEY, and CORECRUXD_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS. If sync is unset, CE runs local-only by default.
